races.name: North Wales Business Day Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Hoe Joly Smoke
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton are a formidable combination and this 8-year-old goes in first-time tongue-tie; has been off 114 days but returns to Good ground where it has form (1W3P from 4 similar-going runs), and as the only confirmed front-runner, will inherit an uncontested lead — though the STYLE_FIT flag suggests it has been operating out of its most comfortable role in recent runs, tempering confidence slightly.

runners_data.name: Sovereignlightcafe
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby send this 5-year-old back after a 251-day absence which is a significant fitness concern; a natural hold-up horse whose best position at the rear is compromised here by field composition — pushed into a midfield mapping it won't naturally settle into — and its bare form figures (3-8-8 on similar ground) offer limited encouragement.

runners_data.name: Iamyouare
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 6-year-old brings the most relevant recent form in the race, including a win and a second over 2m on Good ground, and amateur claimer Harry Brown (10lb) rides for a stable that has sent out zero winners in the last 14 days; the prominent style is a genuine fit for this race shape and the horse's course-distance profile makes it the most logical threat to the favourite.

runners_data.name: That Old Chestnut
runners_data.note: Henry Daly's 6-year-old has a fade warning attached and has finished 8th and 10th in its only two runs on Good ground, making its going and distance profile concerning; a hold-up horse by nature, it arrives 119 days since last seen and offers little evidence that it can improve sufficiently in this novice context.

runners_data.name: Whinny Houston
runners_data.note: Sheila Lewis's 5-year-old returns just 16 days after its last run but has posted P-0-0 in recent form and carries a finishing fade warning; a hold-up horse by profile, its form figures on Good ground are uniformly poor and there is no compelling tactical or form angle to suggest it can reverse recent trends in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Hoe Joly Smoke is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner novice hurdle and, with no meaningful pressure anticipated, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 2m3½f trip on Good ground at Bangor. Iamyouare, a prominent-racing type, will look to track closely and will be the most likely threat to Hoe Joly Smoke's early supremacy, keeping tabs from second or third. The three hold-up horses — Sovereignlightcafe, That Old Chestnut, and Whinny Houston — are all tagged with finishing concerns or redistribution caveats, meaning genuine sustained late challenges from the rear are unlikely to materialise cleanly. This race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-lead profile: a controlled pace set by Hoe Joly Smoke that rewards horses travelling well in the first two or three, with limited genuine closer ammunition behind. The field holds more hold-up types than can meaningfully deliver from the rear — Sovereignlightcafe is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field composition, and is unlikely to secure a position that suits its natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hoe Joly Smoke Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Hoe Joly Smoke bowls along at a comfortable tempo unchallenged and Iamyouare cannot sustain pressure over the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Hoe Joly Smoke settles in front under Harry Skelton, sets a fair but unhurried pace, and the Dan Skelton yard's superior jumping experience at this trip proves decisive in a race run to suit the leader. Iamyouare is best-placed to give chase but may lack the class ceiling to reel in a horse in control of its own destiny at Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent War Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Iamyouare presses Hoe Joly Smoke aggressively from the outset, creating a faster-than-expected tempo that drains both.
scenarios.body: A genuine battle up front would compromise Hoe Joly Smoke's stamina reserves and open the door for a fast-finishing hold-up horse, though the closers in this field carry significant question marks about their ability to deliver in that role. Iamyouare, who has the form, course-distance profile, and amateur jockey confidence, could still emerge as the dominant force if the front two burn each other off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and Sovereignlightcafe or That Old Chestnut finds a clear run to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a faster-run race than the pace map projects and genuine staying power from horses that carry fade warnings and redistribution caveats — both significant obstacles to probability. Sovereignlightcafe has not run for 251 days and That Old Chestnut's limited Good-ground form makes this a low-confidence outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart At Finish
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fatigue cause the front two to capitulate in the closing stages, handing the race to a surviving stayer.
scenarios.body: Whinny Houston and That Old Chestnut have poor recent records and fading profiles, but in a race that disintegrates late they could inherit a placing through attrition rather than merit. This scenario demands multiple mishaps and is the least likely given the quality and experience of Hoe Joly Smoke and Skelton's record at keeping horses competitive.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Iamyouare's prominent style puts immediate pressure on Hoe Joly Smoke at the start — if Mr Harry Brown commits hard from flag-fall, the tempo could rise sharply and undermine the favourite's control.

Sovereignlightcafe returns after 251 days off and is a natural hold-up horse awkwardly placed by field composition — monitor whether Patrick Wadge attempts to push forward rather than drop to the rear, as that tactical friction could disrupt early order.

Both That Old Chestnut and Whinny Houston carry confirmed fade warnings — if either makes a significant move between the third-last and second-last hurdle without sustaining it, they could cause interference for horses travelling behind them.
Hoe Joly Smoke runs in a first-time tongue-tie — watch its early jumping and whether the headgear change produces noticeably sharper or more erratic jumping behaviour in the opening mile.

races.name: Genesis Wealth Management Novices' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Soldier In Mayo
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with a winning return from 475 days off last time (good ground, 20f), handled well by apprentice Theo Gillard; Donald McCain yard has been quiet recently (0/10 in 14 days) but this horse's ability to lead and control tempo is the defining tactical factor of the whole race.
runners_data.comment: Soldier In Mayo is a winner in his last four starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 102 putting him narrowly top-ranked on this evidence — but 475 days off the track is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: My Bobby's Lass
runners_data.note: Lightly raced mare with an excellent record on good ground (8 placings from 10 similar-going starts, two wins), not seen for 436 days so fitness is the key query; Charlie Deutsch booked and tongue-tie applied, but if she returns to something like her best she has the form credentials to trouble any winner from a handy hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Won a start two runs back and has distance and going experience to call upon, but a 436-day absence is a significant query and carrying 167 lb makes life harder for a mare ranked fifth of eight on ratings.

runners_data.name: Barry Fife
runners_data.note: Returned 16 days ago and has placed twice at this track on good ground, though his recent form includes a pull-up and some inconsistent efforts; Gary Hanmer yard has placed one from six in the last fortnight and the jumping record bears watching given the novice context.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back suggests Barry Fife retains ability, and he returns on a quick 16-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going in his favour; winless in his last five starts, but carrying 167 lb, his overall profile appeals here.

runners_data.name: Moonlightinthepark
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose form figures on good ground are thin (just two runs on similar going, no wins or places) and whose recent sequence reads 6-7-9-6-P — form is poor; a genuine hold-up type whose map position understates how far back he will race, and the STYLE_FIT flag appropriately tempers expectations even if pace shapes worked in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up most recently, Moonlightinthepark arrives 158 days fresh and the significant weight of 163 lb looks the chief concern, though she has experience of today's going and our rating suggests she retains ability.

runners_data.name: Rule Me In
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has been consistently placed around the 4th-5th range on good ground without ever winning over fences; Jack Tudor rides but the horse is a true hold-up operator running in a race where the gallop is unlikely to be strong enough to produce the late finishing conditions he needs, tempering his chance accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Rule Me In has run over today's trip and our rating of 98 puts him well clear of his official mark, suggesting he is significantly underestimated; yet to win in his last five starts, and a lengthy 116-day absence plus a hefty 160 lb burden are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Hiero Sport
runners_data.note: Has two wins from 13 runs on similar going and won at 19f in January before a third last time out — arguably the best recent form of the hold-up pack; Jonathan Burke, experienced pilot, but as a natural rear-of-field type he will need a lot to go right in a race where the pace is likely to be controlled and the winning margins small.
runners_data.comment: Hiero Sport unseated last time out, which clouds his recent profile, but he was a winner three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before; the 159 lb burden is the chief concern as he returns after 16 days off.

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: Big handicap slide to OR 73 and a 54-day break for Sam Allwood's yard; placed once in five similar-going starts but has pulled-up and unseated recently — the tongue-tie is applied again and the jumping reliability question is real for a horse whose best result was a second at 21f on good ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of these eight on our figures, Rockvale arrives after an unseating last time and a pull-up three starts back, making him very hard to fancy; experience over today's trip and going, plus 54 days of freshening, are the only crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old has won his last two outings (22f and 19f on good ground) in quick succession, runs just seven days after his latest win, and Harry Skelton takes the ride — the most potent trainer-jockey combination in the field by some distance; a natural hold-up horse in terms of mapping but his recent momentum and youth may see him travel more prominently than his label suggests.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Delgany Second Now is hard to fancy at the weights despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts; he has run over today's going before, and the trainer is firing at 43% over the past fortnight, but the burden of 144 lb is a significant concern.

races.paceDynamic: Soldier In Mayo is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novices' handicap chase and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he is expected to bowl along at a controlled, measured gallop over 2m4½f on good ground at Bangor. The field is unusually loaded with hold-up types — Moonlightinthepark, Rule Me In, Hiero Sport, Rockvale, and Delgany Second Now all prefer to race from the rear, meaning the mid-to-late stages will feature a mass of horses making their move simultaneously rather than any sustained pressure on the leader through the early and middle sections. My Bobby's Lass and Barry Fife will track from off the pace but neither is likely to hustle Soldier In Mayo into an injudicious gallop. This race shape strongly favours the lone front-runner and any horse capable of travelling prominently without getting into a fight for position — sustainable fractions on good ground over this trip at Bangor suit a relaxed, well-placed jumper who can dictate tempo and quicken away from the last. The field holds materially more hold-up horses than can all settle into their natural rear-of-field position; of those redistributed, Delgany Second Now (Harry Skelton, in-form Skelton yard, recent consecutive wins) and Hiero Sport are the most likely to forge closer than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soldier In Mayo Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Soldier In Mayo sets an uncontested, controlled gallop and the hold-up pack fail to reel him in from the last fence.
scenarios.body: Soldier In Mayo bowls along in front on a comfortable lead, jumps fluently, and with no rival to press him through the middle stages he dictates every yard of the contest; on good ground over this trip his jumping efficiency becomes a weapon rather than a liability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Soldier In Mayo in second or third looms alongside at the second-last and outstays him up the run-in.
scenarios.body: My Bobby's Lass or Delgany Second Now, travelling smoothly just off the pace, presses the leader from three out and the sustained challenge breaks Soldier In Mayo's rhythm late; the winner here is one who travels with cover and can produce a clean jump at the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Collects
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is fast enough to soften the principals and a late-running hold-up horse finishes strongest from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Hiero Sport or Rule Me In, given a patient ride and settling into their natural rhythm despite the crowded field, launch a sustained run from the final mile; this scenario requires the front end to have gone hard enough to come back — unlikely but possible on good ground with a solo front-runner setting his own fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition And Errors
scenarios.trigger: If the jumping test produces casualties, unseaters, or significant errors that reshuffle the race entirely in the final mile.
scenarios.body: In a novice chasing context with Barry Fife's jumping record (pulled-up recently) and several inexperienced fencers in the pack, errors at key fences could open the door to whoever survives cleanest; the winner under this scenario is the most reliable jumper left standing rather than the fastest finisher.

watchPoints.text: Soldier In Mayo's jumping must be monitored from the first fence — if he makes early errors he surrenders the positional advantage that makes him dangerous and the race shape collapses entirely.

Delgany Second Now ran just seven days ago; watch the pre-race ring to assess freshness, as a quick turnaround for a four-year-old novice chaser over 2m4½f on a track new to him carries physical risk despite his form.

Barry Fife's jumping record includes a recent pull-up and his form figures in similar company are inconsistent — watch him at the fences in the back straight where Bangor's chase track can expose novice errors.

The mass of hold-up horses (five runners tagged as redistributed) means the final bend could be congested as they all simultaneously ask for their effort — watch for traffic problems between the last two fences that could benefit whoever is out in front.

My Bobby's Lass returns from 436 days off; watch her in the preliminary stages and early in the race for any sign she has retained condition — if she travels sweetly through the first mile her good-ground record makes her a significant threat late.

races.name: Goffs Yorton Sale 10th September Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Sure Touch
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in fine heart having won over good ground at 22f, handled by apprentice Lewis Saunders (5lb claim useful at the weights); 40 days since last run is not a concern for Olly Murphy's yard, but he needs a truly run race to deliver his late effort and a slow Presentandcounting gallop may leave him with too much to do.|
runners_data.comment: Sure Touch brings solid recent form to the table — a winner three starts back and third two starts back — and has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; a 40-day break is the main unknown.

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: James Bowen takes the ride for his father Mickey and the combination has strong recent form — four wins and a second from the last five, all on good or good-to-soft ground; naturally prominent and well suited to sitting a length or two off a single pace-setter, and the move up to 3m at Bangor on good ground looks well within range.|
runners_data.comment: Tamarind Bay arrives on the back of back-to-back wins before that unseating last time, and with experience of today's going he is firmly in the mix carrying 163 lb; the weight is the one factor to watch.

runners_data.name: Homme Public
runners_data.note: Consistent without being prolific at Grade level, finishing third over good ground on his last two starts at similar trips; Jack Tudor is a sharp jockey who will place him off the pace, but the headgear (tongue-tie, visor) suggests connections are trying to sharpen focus and the lack of a recent win is a mild concern heading into this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Homme Public shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here in solid freshness just 12 days on, his experience over today's going a useful asset; winless in his last five starts, but our rating marks him as the one to beat on 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Four wins from his last five starts is a striking record and all came on good ground, making this surface a clear ally; Ben Jones partners a horse who is naturally prominent and has already beaten horses rated in this OR band, giving him strong claims to repeat the trick by travelling fluidly behind Presentandcounting and striking from the penultimate fence.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Regal Renaissance faces a stiff ask under 155 lb, yet her recent record is eye-catching — third last time out after three consecutive wins, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Presentandcounting
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 12-year-old has dominated the pace role in similar fields with an exceptional 14-of-15 run record on good ground, and carrying the lowest weight at 150lbs is a tangible advantage; he will not be headed early and Theo Gillard's job is simply to jump him fluently and preserve his gallop — the danger is that his control of tempo benefits those immediately behind him more than himself.|
runners_data.comment: Presentandcounting has been knocking on the door, finishing third last time out, third two starts back, and a second three starts back, with our rating of 124 marking him out as a leading player under 150 lb; the chief concern is 53 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Enters with five wins from his last six and a 9/21 yard strike rate in the 14-day window is strong, but Thickthorn Tom's natural style is to race from the rear and he is unlikely to find that position with Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance also in the field; the tongue-tie is noted, and Harry Skelton's quality is not in question, but racing beyond his preferred hold-up position in an already compact field materially tempers confidence in his form figures translating.|
runners_data.comment: Thickthorn Tom arrives in cracking nick — a winner three of his last four starts, last seen just eight days ago, with experience of today's trip and conditions — but he ranks last of six on our figures and carries 149 lb, making it hard to fancy at these weights despite the trainer firing at 43%.

races.paceDynamic: Presentandcounting is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no other horse likely to press him hard from the outset, he should be able to control tempo from the front over the full 3m at Bangor on good ground. Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance are the prominent types most likely to track him closely from early on, forming a compact lead group that sets a manageable, rhythm-based gallop rather than a searching test. Behind them, Sure Touch and Homme Public will look to travel in rear and produce their efforts late, while Thickthorn Tom — a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to mapped midfield — is unlikely to find the same position at the back that his form demands, which tempers his chance in a shape that suits closers. The tactical verdict is clear: with a single honest pace-setter controlling an uncontested gallop on a fair surface, this race shape most strongly favours prominent racers who can travel within themselves behind Presentandcounting and produce a fluent jumping challenge from two out, rewarding Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance above the true hold-up types. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear, and Thickthorn Tom is the one most likely to find himself racing out of his natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Presentandcounting leads at a controlled gallop and the prominent duo of Tamarind Bay and Regal Renaissance track smoothly throughout.
scenarios.body: Presentandcounting sets an uncontested pace that flatters horses travelling on his heels, and with no pressure forcing a sprint, those positioned just off the lead have the energy reserves to assert from the second-last fence; good-ground form for both protagonists adds confidence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Presentandcounting dictates an unusually slow tempo, controls every fence cleanly and simply outstays the field up the straight.
scenarios.body: At 12 years old Presentandcounting carries the lowest weight and has an outstanding record of placing in similar good-ground chases, and a dawdle that nullifies the closers' finishing kicks plays directly into his ability to jump and gallop relentlessly; only a dramatic stamina collapse in the final half-mile would stop him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string out the field and the closers have clear daylight to produce a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Sure Touch has a winning run over good ground at a similar trip and brings hold-up credentials, while Homme Public has placed at three miles on good before; however both must find more than their recent form suggests and depend on a stronger gallop than one lone pace-setter is likely to create.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or a rough-and-tumble race of fallers reduces the field and creates a lottery finish.
scenarios.body: With six runners over 3m of fences, any jumping mishap at a crucial point — particularly in the lead group — could hand the initiative to whoever survives intact; Thickthorn Tom, despite likely racing out of his natural hold-up role, has raw winning form and the Skelton yard's recent 14-day strike rate could see him capitalise on a depleted field.

watchPoints.text: Thickthorn Tom has won five of his last six but is a genuine hold-up horse likely to be forced into a midfield position that does not suit — watch whether Harry Skelton can find enough cover or whether the horse gets competitive and races too freely.

Presentandcounting's control of tempo is the pivot of the entire race: if he sets a very slow gallop the closers (Sure Touch, Homme Public) may never get into it — watch the pace from the first fence to judge whether the hold-up horses are viable.
Regal Renaissance has a very strong recent record but jumps up in trip to 3m today for the first time in this sequence — watch his jumping in the final mile to see if stamina becomes an issue.

Tamarind Bay ran only 20 days ago and carries the second-highest weight in the field at 163lbs; monitor his jumping fluency early to gauge whether fatigue or the burden affects his prominent racing style in the closing stages.

The going report confirms Good across all seven races at Bangor today — conditions are genuinely consistent, so any runner whose trainer entered specifically for this surface (particularly Presentandcounting's 14/15 good-ground record) should be taken at face value.

races.name: Du Construction Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has won once and placed twice in eight similar-going starts, trained by Alan King in fine recent form (1 win from 9 over 14 days); races prominently and will lead uncontested here, which suits him ideally, though his recent form figures of 166-42 suggest he finds rivals coming at him at the finish.
runners_data.comment: Ernest Gray shaped with plenty of promise when second last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, giving him solid each-way claims; the main concern is a hefty 164 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Roger Pol
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's 8-year-old has a solid record on good ground (4 wins and 7 places from 15 similar-going runs) but his natural hold-up style means he needs the pace to be strong enough to bring him into contention; Isabelle Ryder claims 5lb which helps the weight, and 40 days between runs is not a concern given his form string includes a recent win.
runners_data.comment: Roger Pol is the top-rated runner here and his win five starts back gives him the most recent winning form in this line-up; he has run over today's trip and going, and while his last four outings have been below that level, he enters on a fresh 40-day break that could spark a revival.

runners_data.name: Secret Trix
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's consistent 9-year-old sports tongue strap and has been remarkably placed of late — form reads 23-322 with all five recent runs in the money — but is a hold-up performer who requires a genuine gallop to unlock his late run; Tom Hutsby's 10lb claim softens the burden, yet the steady pace expected here is unlikely to play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but a model of consistency with three seconds and two thirds, Secret Trix has experience of today's trip and going and our rating puts him right among the principals; the concern is whether he can convert his habitual placing form into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Kiwi de Cotte
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 6-year-old is the most interesting prominent racer in the field with two wins and three places from four runs on good ground; Harry Skelton takes over in the saddle and the horse's young age and fresh legs (20 days since last run) give him a live each-way profile sitting just off Ernest Gray, though he does carry the highest-profile jockey booking in this race.
runners_data.comment: Kiwi de Cotte arrives on the back of a win last time out, boasts a pulled-up blot aside three wins in his last five starts, and handles today's distance and going; the main concern is a hefty 159 lb to shoulder.

runners_data.name: Speed Davis
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 8-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature whose true running style places him further back than the midfield position the map shows — he is unlikely to find his ideal slot in a five-runner field at a steady pace; the trainer has drawn a blank over 14 days (0 from 10) and the form figures of 611-56 show his last two runs were well below his winning level, making his profile the hardest to make a case for today.
runners_data.comment: Speed Davis has finished sixth and fifth in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy ranked last on our figures, though he did win three and four starts back and has experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Ernest Gray is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Kiwi de Cotte as a genuine prominent challenger, he faces no serious early pressure and should be permitted to set a comfortable, controlled gallop throughout. Kiwi de Cotte (Harry Skelton) will track closely in second, creating a compact two-horse lead group that dictates a steady, sustainable tempo over this 2m7f trip on good ground. The hold-up trio of Roger Pol, Secret Trix, and Speed Davis will be strung out behind, though Speed Davis — a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map — is unlikely to find the true rear position his style demands, meaning the closers' end of the field is less straightforward than it appears. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who travel into an honest gallop and quicken off it, rather than late finishers asked to make up ground against a front end that will never be overhauled at a sprint finish in a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Sets Up Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If Ernest Gray dictates a measured gallop and Kiwi de Cotte tracks him closely throughout, the race is run entirely to suit horses who travel prominently.
scenarios.body: Ernest Gray leads at his own pace with Kiwi de Cotte poised just off his quarters, and the combination of good ground and a manageable tempo means both are travelling well into the straight; the hold-up horses are asked a question too late over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front pair push along hard enough to compromise each other and the pace becomes genuinely strong, the closers get a proper target to hunt down.
scenarios.body: Roger Pol and Secret Trix, both proven on good ground and consistent at this sort of trip, would be the primary beneficiaries of a stronger-than-expected gallop that finds out the leaders inside the final two flights; their superior late reserves become a genuine weapon.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Skelton Jockey Move Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Skelton times Kiwi de Cotte's challenge to perfection and Ernest Gray fades from the front in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Kiwi de Cotte's strong recent form — four runs on good ground all producing respectable finishes including two wins — combined with the Skelton team's proven tactical acumen could see him sweep past a tiring leader in the straight; the 6-year-old's youth and freshness after only 20 days since his last run could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart through a tactical muddle, jumping errors, or a significant incident that scrambles the expected running order.
scenarios.body: Speed Davis, though a genuine hold-up type who will struggle to find his natural position in this small field, carries form figures of 1-1 within the last year and could theoretically capitalise on a chaotic scenario; the low-mileage field of just five runners makes a clean race likely, keeping this scenario at the margins.

watchPoints.text: Ernest Gray has dominated the early pace map but his recent form figures (166-42) suggest he gets caught close home — watch whether Tom Cannon allows him to coast or is forced to up the tempo to hold Kiwi de Cotte off entering the straight.

Kiwi de Cotte shaped with promise last time but has pulled up once (the P in his form) and is a young horse over 2m7f for the first time — watch his jumping under Harry Skelton, particularly if he is keen early tracking the leader.

Speed Davis is physically a hold-up horse racing in a small field at a likely steady pace, which means he may find himself shuffled wider and closer to the pace than suits him — watch his position at the halfway point as a clue to whether he can get competitive.

Roger Pol has a strong place record on good ground but has not won since finishing first at 24f on good; the combination of his age (8), hold-up style, and the likely steady tempo means watch whether Isabelle Ryder (5lb claimer) attempts to push forward earlier than usual to compensate.

Secret Trix's tongue strap is back on after consistent placed efforts — if the gallop is genuinely strong rather than crawling, her late runs become viable; she is the one hold-up horse whose form consistency gives her a realistic chance if the pace scenario shifts.

races.name: Kinsey Anniversary Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Jammy Jay
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 98 and has placed on good ground in five of her last six attempts, suggesting she handles conditions well; a genuine hold-up type who will be further back than ideal in a small, slowly-run field — her chance depends on Northern Rose weakening late.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and third five starts back, Jammy Jay has run over today's trip and going and steps up as the top-rated runner here; winless in her last five, she will need to find more, but at 168 lb she remains a clear benchmark for this field.

runners_data.name: I Heard A Rumour
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combine and the horse arrives on a lengthy 171-day absence, which is the key concern; a natural deep hold-up type who will be anchored at the back of this small field, and racing out of position relative to the pace shape makes winning difficult — the layoff adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her latest start and yet to win in her last three, I Heard A Rumour nonetheless brings distance experience and a red-hot trainer firing at 43% over the past fortnight; the main concern is 171 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor is a strong booking and the four-year-old arrives in form having won two of her last four starts, all on good ground at 2m; she wears a tongue-tie and is a hold-up type who will need to be ridden more prominently than usual in this field — her recent winning form makes her the strongest challenger to Northern Rose if she can track close enough.
runners_data.comment: Prettylady arrives here a winner three starts back, and again four starts back, giving her a strong recent profile over today's trip and going; the concern is that ninth on her latest outing leaves something to prove returning from 40 days off under a big 157 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and tongue-tie combination suggesting she can be free or reluctant to settle; she is a true hold-up horse who will find herself dragged closer to the pace than she likes in this six-runner field, and her OR of 83 alongside modest recent form (three finishes outside the frame from four runs) limits her appeal.
runners_data.comment: Rated 92 and ranked second in the field, Daring To Dream brings solid credentials to this contest, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is a winless recent run of five starts, and 153 lb is a stiff burden to overcome after 48 days off.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will go straight to the front unchallenged; she has excellent good-ground form (15 runs on good, one win and eight places) and returns on a sharp 15-day turnaround suggesting she is in a productive spell — her style-fit tag reflects only that she is slightly off her very best role, but here she owns the pace.
runners_data.comment: Northern Rose has shown she can win, landing a victory two starts back, but finishes of seventh last time out and a ranking of fifth of six on our figures make her hard to fancy here, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns fit on just 15 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield-trained seven-year-old who returns on just 10 days' rest; she is a genuine hold-up type whose best ground stats (one win, one place from nine runs on good) are uninspiring, and being pushed into midfield by a crowded hold-up division compounds the challenge — lowest OR in the field at 75.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Miss Fedora faces a stiff task here; two pulled-up efforts in recent form are a concern, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, she will set a sustainable, controlled gallop from the outset on good ground at Bangor. The pace is unlikely to be fierce — a single front-runner allowed to bowl along unchallenged typically produces a moderate tempo that suits horses who can sit close to the action rather than those asking questions from the back. Jammy Jay, Prettylady, I Heard A Rumour, Daring To Dream, and Miss Fedora are all natural hold-up or deep hold-up types, meaning a small, contained field of six will see several of them forced closer to the pace than they would ideally choose. This race shape — one uncontested leader, modest gallop, compact field — heavily favours prominent and close-tracking profiles who can exploit the steady tempo and attack from a handy position, rather than genuine closers who need a searching pace to generate momentum from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Northern Rose Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Rose is allowed to dictate an uncontested lead at a comfortable clip and the field does not collectively quicken on her.
scenarios.body: Northern Rose bowls along in front, the moderate gallop keeps the race falsely run and she is never seriously pressured, turning for home with a decisive advantage; her recent course form on good going and her headgear (tongue-tie/pull-through) suggest she handles these conditions well and her prominent style is perfectly suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough for a horse tracking in second or third to produce a winning late surge past Northern Rose.
scenarios.body: A runner sitting a length or two off Northern Rose's shoulder conserves energy through a steady gallop before producing a decisive jump at the last hurdle and pulling clear on the run-in; Prettylady, with her two recent wins and positive course form on good ground, is the most naturally equipped to execute this move from a handy position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a hold-up horse finds an unobstructed run to the line from the back.
scenarios.body: The moderate tempo means hold-up types carry too much ground to make up, but if Northern Rose ties up dramatically on the run-in a closer could appear late; Jammy Jay has the highest OR in the field and her good-going form (two places from three runs on good) gives her the best chance of capitalising if a gap appears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Rose sets an unusually slow tempo that produces a sprint finish where fitness and class separate the field.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling gallop compresses the field entirely, turning the race into a flat-out dash from two out; in this shape OR and fitness of the freshest, classiest runner matters most, and Jammy Jay's higher rating edges an argument though no runner is ideally profiled for a pure sprint test.

watchPoints.text: Northern Rose (James Davies) — watch whether she is allowed to stride out unchallenged from the off; if she gets a soft lead she could prove very hard to reel in before the last.

Prettylady — watch her early position; if Jack Tudor can place her within two lengths of Northern Rose rather than being buried in a bunch, her recent winning form makes her the most dangerous threat in the field.

I Heard A Rumour — 171 days off the track is a significant concern; watch for any signs of race-rustiness early, particularly at the hurdles, which would confirm she is essentially a non-runner for winning purposes today.

Jammy Jay — watch whether Ben Poste attempts to position her closer than her natural style suggests, given the small field; if she is still four or more lengths adrift entering the back straight the steady pace is likely to count against her.

Miss Fedora and Daring To Dream — watch for crowding on the first bend with five hold-up types in a six-runner field; a bump or shuffle-back early could effectively end any winning chance for either runner before the race has properly started.

races.name: Lexus Wrexham Open 2026 Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Harrys Hope
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Ben Pauling with excellent good-ground profile (11 of 15 sim-going runs in frame); over a trip he handles well and returning on a sharp 16-day turnaround with cheekpieces, he is positioned to stalk the leaders and hit the line hard.
runners_data.comment: Harrys Hope has been knocking on the door with three seconds in her last five starts, and returning after just 16 days she looks fit and ready; she has run over today's trip and going before, and carrying 170 lb, she is the one to beat off a mark of 112.

runners_data.name: Post Chaise
runners_data.note: Toby Wynne takes the ride for Greenall & Guerriero on a horse returning from a huge 554-day absence; his one win came on soft and all five recent runs are on soft, so this good ground is an untested variable, though the trip and OR of 110 give him a class edge if fit.
runners_data.comment: Post Chaise franked his winning form with a runner-up finish last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat at the head of this field; the concern is 554 days off the track, and he will need to prove that rustiness is no issue carrying 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Ridin Solo
runners_data.note: A consistent placer for Donald McCain — three placed runs from four on good and a win on soft — who will race prominently off the pace in his natural style; McCain has been quiet in the 14-day window (0/10) which tempers confidence slightly but the horse has form over this distance.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and eyecatching in his last three starts — third two runs back and second last time out — Ridin Solo arrives as a strong threat if his 83-day absence hasn't blunted his edge, though he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with an outstanding good-ground record (10 of 11 runs on similar going, 2 wins, 5 places); Jonathan Burke will send him straight to the front and his last win came over 18f, so stamina over this extended 3m trip is the one question mark on his strongest surface.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a winner five starts back, Back In The Bay has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 108 marks her as a serious threat carrying 159 lb; the main concern is her trainer's wretched recent strike-rate of just 1 from 35.

runners_data.name: Depalma
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this seven-year-old for a Skelton yard in form (9/21 over 14 days); running style is hold-up and sim-going record shows zero wins or places on good, which is a concern — he has missed the frame on good in all seven attempts in those conditions despite being well-handled.
runners_data.comment: Depalma showed a win and four placed efforts in his last five starts, and has experience of today's going in his favour, but he arrives 110 days since his last run and is ranked sixth of eight, making him a speculative each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Second confirmed front-runner, returning quickly on 13 days for Nick Scholfield, with two wins and ten places from 15 sim-going runs — remarkably consistent on good ground; he will fight for the lead with Back In The Bay and his staying profile over 3m Bangor suits a grinding contest, though he may lack the resolution to pass rivals at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in his last five starts, Limerick Leader has been placed third two starts back and second four starts back, but that elusive first win continues to escape him; experience over today's trip and going, plus a quick 13-day turnaround, keep him interesting under 154 lb.

runners_data.name: Royal Time
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor rides this Christian Williams seven-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse in form terms but is mapped to midfield due to the surplus of hold-up types in this field; he unseated last time, returned to form with a 4th on good, and his best chance depends on a strongly run race — a style-fit discount (0.92) applies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Royal Time faces a stiff task here; an unseated rider in recent form does little to inspire confidence, though he has experience of today's going and returns after 106 days off.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Max Young's gelding has been placed 15 times on similar going without a win and is another true hold-up horse that the race shape pushes forward on the map; carrying the lowest weight (142lbs) offers a theoretical advantage but his persistent tendency to finish mid-pack without winning limits expectation here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Bahtiyar faces a stiff task off 142 lb, and 54 days between runs adds to the concern; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a second three starts back offers the sole crumb of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over this 3m Bangor trip, creating an honest, pressured gallop on good ground with neither likely to give way willingly. Post Chaise and Ridin Solo will push up prominently into the slipstream, meaning the early order will be genuinely competitive and the pace sustained throughout rather than falsely dawdling. This race shape — a genuinely run 3m on good ground with multiple pace angles — classically suits hold-up horses who can travel sweetly off the tempo and produce a late, measured challenge, making Harrys Hope and Depalma the profile types to concentrate on. This field contains more hold-up horses than the rear of the field can naturally accommodate; Royal Time and Bahtiyar are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, and in practice Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader are most likely to actually secure the front two positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest pace, stayers grind
scenarios.trigger: If Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader set a genuine contested gallop that grinds rivals into the turf from three out
scenarios.body: The sustained tempo over 3m on good ground burns off the prominent types and leaves the race to genuine stayers who can switch gears late; Harrys Hope, with strong good-ground form and a hold-up style, is ideally placed to pick off the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front two dominate unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace setters gains a clear break mid-race and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap from the third last
scenarios.body: Back In The Bay, with ten runs on good ground and strong course-form, is the likelier of the two pace men to convert a front-running break into a winning effort if rivals idle in behind; Limerick Leader's consistent placing record on good ground makes him the natural second string in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent types swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures or the front two tire quickly, allowing Post Chaise or Ridin Solo to take over from a stalking position at the second last
scenarios.body: Post Chaise's return from 554 days off is a clear unknown but he has winning form on good and this trip suits; Ridin Solo has been consistently placed at Bangor-level distances and could benefit if given a soft lead from a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fierce and all front-rankers stop, allowing a late-running type to sweep through
scenarios.body: Royal Time and Bahtiyar are the natural beneficiaries in this shape but both are mapped out of their true hold-up role and face the challenge of travelling mid-division rather than off the back; their discounted STYLE_FIT tempers confidence in this scenario and it requires an unusually strong pace collapse to land.

watchPoints.text: Back In The Bay and Limerick Leader — watch whether they genuinely fight for the lead from the first fence; if either concedes early, the pace scenario collapses and the whole race map shifts.
Post Chaise — 554 days off the track is a major fitness unknown; if he runs flat from a prominent position it opens the race wide for the hold-up horses behind him.
Depalma — Harry Skelton's booking is eye-catching and the yard is in form, but zero places from seven runs on good ground is a persistent pattern that cannot be ignored if he is to outrun his odds.

Royal Time — watch his jumping at the first few fences; if he is slow or untidy early, he will lose his midfield mapping entirely and race further back than intended, making his redistribution position even less natural.

Harrys Hope — monitor his position turning for home; if Ben Jones has him covered up in the last group of horses approaching the third last, the 3m trip and sustained gallop should bring him into the race exactly when his rivals tire.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Bobby Socks
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here; Sean Quinlan has ridden the horse before and the Lizzie Quinlan yard sends her in form (1 win from 6 in 14 days), but her last outing was 83 days ago and she has been running over shorter distances — the step back to 2m3½f Good is manageable and she gets the run of the race from the front.

runners_data.name: Faded Fantasy
runners_data.note: Amateur jockey Mr J J Murphy-Knight (7lb claim) partners this hold-up mare who has been hitting a wall late in her last five runs, including three fifths; Good going suits on paper but her finishes suggest she rarely gets to the winner and the Christian Williams yard is out of form (0 from 5 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Present Fair
runners_data.note: Donald McCain handler is 0 from 10 in the last 14 days, a stark stat; holds-up and needs a true gallop to produce her best, as evidenced by a 15th last time out, though her Good-ground form does include a win over this trip at Bangor.
runners_data.comment: Present Fair won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with our rating of 102 putting him second among the 12 runners; the worry is that he has been out of the placings in three of his last four outings.

runners_data.name: La Lolita
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at 163lbs with James Bowen aboard; has run five times on Good going and placed in four of them, is consistent in form (four recent finishes of 3-1-5-4) and at only 12 days since her last run is race-fit — Gary Hanmer's stable sent out a winner in the 14-day window.
runners_data.comment: La Lolita won four starts back and has since finished third three starts back, though back-to-back fourth and fifth placed efforts have taken the shine off. She has distance and going experience, returns fit on 12 days' rest, but 163 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Eyeeye
runners_data.note: Settles at the rear by instinct and genuinely fades late — the flagged finishing concern is supported by a form string that includes a 17th — pushed into a midfield map position here simply because the field has too many hold-up horses; the 0.91 style-fit score tempers expectations considerably.
runners_data.comment: Eyeeye arrives here 15 days after his last outing and has run over today's going, though he is winless in his last five starts and comes off an unplaced effort; a second four starts back offers some encouragement, but 162 lb is a stern ask for a gelding rated 94.

runners_data.name: Ballynoe Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good six runs ago and has placed three times in similar conditions; Nicky Richards sends him out 20 days fresh, but his natural hold-up style means he'll be further back than ideal in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring him with a late run.
runners_data.comment: Ballynoe Boy landed a win in his last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he carries 162 lb and ranks eighth of twelve on ratings, making him a solid mid-division type rather than an obvious winner.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this lightly raced four-year-old for the in-form Dan Skelton yard (9 from 21 in 14 days); has won over 16f on Good and placed at 18f, with the step up to 19f likely to suit — he travels prominently in his races and this is the profile that benefits from a Bobby Socks-controlled gallop.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out following a win two starts back, Ashdown Forest brings distance and going experience to this, and a trainer firing at 43% over the past fortnight is a useful ally; however, carrying 161 lb and ranked seventh of twelve on ratings gives this gelding plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Lord Cauvelliere
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by nature whose five-run sequence at 16-17f on Good shows he regularly finishes mid-pack (4th best effort); the step up in trip to 2m3½f is untested, and with a hood on and a modest OR of 88, his redistribution into midfield reflects a race too crowded at the rear rather than an inclination to race there.
runners_data.comment: Lord Cauvelliere has strong claims on his rating of 99 — 11 lb clear of his official mark — and returns on a quick turnaround having run over today's going before, yet the worry is a consistent failure to convert, winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Cappa Lass
runners_data.note: Raced just three times visible in the data, all on Good, finishing 6th-7th-8th — a flat, unimpressive recent record; Jack Tudor rides but she has been off 111 days and her typical hold-up style will leave her exposed in a race unlikely to produce the pace she needs, despite the Greenall/Guerriero yard having a winner in the 14-day window.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Cappa Lass shaped with promise when second four starts back, though she has been winless in her last four outings and returns after 111 days off carrying 151 lb.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Cracker
runners_data.note: Consistently placed at 16-17f on Good and showed a 3rd last time, wearing a tongue-tie and a pads combination; her natural instinct to hold-up means Toby Wynne will have to position her further forward than she'd like — she has the fitness (48 days off) but the style mismatch will cost her ground at the critical moment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Cawthorne Cracker arrives 48 days fresh carrying 146 lb, though he does have experience of today's distance and going, and a third three starts back offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Dante's Inferno
runners_data.note: Off 111 days, the longest absence in the field; has been placing regularly (3rd, 4th, 4th, 4th) without winning, typically racing hold-up, and Jonathan Burke will find a race dominated by a steady gallop unhelpful for a horse who needs strong sectionals to finish through — OR 76 also makes weight-carrying less straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Dante's Inferno faces a stiff task here, returning from a 111-day absence carrying 144 lb; a third four starts back offers slim encouragement, but that seventh last time out is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Lucky In Taipan
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's yard is in fine form (3 from 6 in 14 days) and Ben Jones takes the ride; however, a 13th last time out on Soft and a form string including a P (pulled up) suggests inconsistency, and a true hold-up profile displaced into midfield means he will need a dramatic change in fortune to feature at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Lucky In Taipan is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 142 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and at least showed a shade of form with a third last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Bobby Socks is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press her for the lead on Good ground over 2m3½f at Bangor, she can dictate an honest but uncontested gallop throughout. The substantial majority of this field are true hold-up types by nature — Eyeeye, Ballynoe Boy, Lord Cauvelliere, Cappa Lass, Cawthorne Cracker, Dante's Inferno and Lucky In Taipan are all genuine rear-of-field horses who cannot all settle in their preferred position and several will be shuffled into midfield against their instincts. With pace-pressure minimal and a clear lead available, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from a close-up position before the final two hurdles, rather than those needing a strong end-to-end gallop to bring them into contention from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bobby Socks Front Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bobby Socks dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the field trails in a strung-out line.
scenarios.body: Bobby Socks rolls along at her own pace on Good ground she handles, setting a rhythm that suits prominent racers who can simply track and pounce, while true hold-up horses in the rear struggle to land a late blow without the strong pace they need.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that close-up tracking horses swoop past Bobby Socks approaching the last and the race becomes a battle between those who raced handy.
scenarios.body: With a gentle gallop, the horses who travel in the first half-dozen have all the energy conserved at the finish; true hold-up horses forced to cover ground from midfield arrive too late to threaten those already in position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the gallop becomes genuinely strong enough to string the field, opening a gap for a hold-up horse to close.
scenarios.body: This is the shape least likely to materialise given Bobby Socks is solitary at the head and unlikely to be pressured, but a genuine horse who gets a true test could pick off tiring front-runners; those redistributed from hold-up roles face the added burden of racing out of position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make aggressive moves to close early, disrupting Bobby Socks's rhythm and causing a bunching finish.
scenarios.body: A chaotic mid-race surge from the crowded midfield could result in a messy finish over the final two hurdles; horses with reliable jumping and tactical flexibility cope best when the pattern breaks down unpredictably.

watchPoints.text: Bobby Socks (Sean Quinlan) has an uncontested lead and could exploit it fully — watch whether she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged from the second hurdle, as that scenario makes her very difficult to peg back.

Ashdown Forest (Harry Skelton/Dan Skelton) is the sharpest danger if he travels prominently as expected — watch whether Skelton positions him within striking range of Bobby Socks by the top of the straight, as that is the profile this race shape rewards.

La Lolita (James Bowen) is fit off 12 days and her Good-ground form is consistent — if she gets a prominent pitch early rather than being blocked in by the congested midfield, she is capable of asserting between the last two hurdles.

The crowded mid-to-rear group — Eyeeye, Ballynoe Boy, Lord Cauvelliere, Cappa Lass, Cawthorne Cracker, Dante's Inferno and Lucky In Taipan — will all be jostling for the same space with none able to occupy their natural rear position; watch for traffic issues and interference approaching the fourth-last hurdle.

Ballynoe Boy (Danny McMenamin/Nicky Richards) is the most interesting of the redistributed hold-up horses given he won six runs ago on Good; if the pace somehow increases mid-race and he finds daylight turning for home, he represents the most credible latecomer threat in the field.
